newsitem.title: INDIA: India proposes cutting duties on steel inputs.
newsitem.headline: India proposes cutting duties on steel inputs.

text.p: India on Friday proposed cutting the customs import duty on inputs for the steel industry including coking coal, nickel, ferro alloys and re-rollable steel.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, in the government's 1997/98 (April-March) budget, proposed cutting the duty on coking coal of ash content below 12 percent to three percent from five percent.
The duty on coking coal of higher ash content, as well as coke, would be cut to 10 percent from 20 percent.

He said the government planned to reduce the duty on re-rollable steel scrap to 20 percent from 30 percent, the duty on nickel to 10 percent from 20, and the duty on ferroalloys to 20 percent from 25 percent.
Chidambaram said the cuts should help the steel industry to reduce output costs.

He also proposed cutting the duty on cold rolled coils of iron and steel to 25 percent from 30 to help the engineering industry. The duty on ships which are imported for dismantling would be cut to five percent from 10 and on pig iron to 10 percent from 20.
Chidambaram said to help the power sector, the duty on coking coal would be cut to 10 percent from 20.
